info.title: dian-einvoice
info.description:
The API of dian-einvoice, the same one its web app uses: contacts, items, invoices, credit and debit notes, their electronic document chain (UBL 2.1 XML, CUFE or CUDE, XAdES signature, transmission and the answer), the delivery to the customer, and payments. In this project the DIAN is always a local simulator and every email lands in a local mailbox: nothing reaches the DIAN.

## Authentication

Send an API key of the company in the `Authorization` header: `Authorization: Bearer dei_...`. Owners and admins create keys in **Settings → Developers**; a key is shown once, only its hash is stored, and it can expire or be revoked.

- The company is the company of the key: `X-Company-Id` is not needed and, when sent, must be that company (403 otherwise).
- `read_only` keys read everything below. `read_write` keys also write contacts, items, invoices, notes and payments and run their actions (issue, retry, resend, send again, void a payment).
- No key manages users, API keys, webhooks, certificates, DIAN settings or the simulator: those belong to the web app session, and keys get 403.
- In timelines, the actor of an action done with a key is the key, with its name.

## Idempotency

Any `POST` may carry an `Idempotency-Key` header (1 to 255 visible ASCII characters, such as a UUID). Keys are per company and kept 24 hours with the answer and a fingerprint of the request (method, path and body).

- The same key with the same request returns the first answer, status and body, with `Idempotent-Replayed: true`, and runs nothing.
- The same key with another request answers **422**; while the first request is still running, **409**.
- Reserving a key is atomic, so two simultaneous requests with one key never both run. A 5xx answer is not kept: the request can be repeated with the same key.

## Rate limits

Each key may make 120 requests per minute unless it has a limit of its own. Every answer to a key carries `X-RateLimit-Limit`, `X-RateLimit-Remaining` and `X-RateLimit-Reset` (Unix time), plus `RateLimit-Policy` and `RateLimit` of the IETF draft. Above the limit the API answers **429** with `Retry-After` in seconds.

## Pagination and search

Lists answer `data`, `links` and `meta` (`current_page`, `last_page`, `per_page`, `total`). Use `?page=` and `?per_page=` (1 to 100, 25 by default); most lists also take `?search=` and their own filters.

## Money and dates

Amounts, quantities and rates are decimal strings, such as `"1190000.00"`, never floats. Dates of documents are Colombian dates (`YYYY-MM-DD`); instants are ISO 8601 in UTC.

## Errors

Every error is `application/problem+json` (RFC 9457): `type` (always `about:blank`), `title`, `status`, `detail` and `instance`; validation errors (422) add `errors`, the messages of each field. 401: no valid credentials. 403: the key level or the role does not allow it. 404: not found in the company. 409: the state does not allow it, such as issuing twice. 503: a local service, such as the DIAN simulator, is not answering.

## Webhooks

Owners and admins subscribe URLs in **Settings → Developers** to these events: `invoice.issued`, `invoice.accepted`, `invoice.rejected`, `invoice.failed`, `invoice.delivered`, `invoice.paid`, `invoice.voided`; `credit_note.issued`, `credit_note.accepted`, `credit_note.rejected`, `credit_note.delivered`, and the same four for `debit_note`; `payment.recorded` and `payment.voided`. "Send test event" sends `webhook.test`.

The body is `{"id": "evt_...", "type": "invoice.accepted", "created_at": "...", "company_id": "...", "data": {"object": {...}}}`, where `data.object` is the same resource this API returns for that document or payment.

Deliveries follow the [Standard Webhooks](https://www.standardwebhooks.com) specification: headers `webhook-id` (the event id, the same on every retry), `webhook-timestamp` (Unix seconds) and `webhook-signature` (`v1,` and the base64 HMAC-SHA256 of `{webhook-id}.{webhook-timestamp}.{body}` with the secret, the base64 after `whsec_` decoded). Verify the signature over the raw body, reject old timestamps, and answer 2xx within 5 seconds.

Delivery is at least once and in no particular order: deduplicate by `webhook-id`. A failed attempt is retried after 2, 5, 15, 45 and 120 seconds; then the delivery fails and can be sent again by hand. A subscription is switched off after 20 failed deliveries in a row.

DeliveryStatus.description:
Delivery of an accepted document to its customer, apart from its electronic status. It starts when the local DIAN simulator accepts the document and runs three queued steps (DeliveryStep): pending (attached_document → pdf → email) → delivered | not_applicable any step ↘ failed → pending (Send again, or Regenerate PDF when the PDF failed) delivered | not_applicable → pending (Send again) The email always goes to the local development mailbox in this project: delivered means "the * local mailbox accepted it", and nothing leaves the machine. Drafts and documents not accepted yet have no delivery status. | | |---| | `pending`
Building the AttachedDocument or the PDF, or packaging and sending the email. | | `delivered`
The mail server accepted the email with the zip. | | `failed`
A step failed, or every email attempt did; the reason is kept with the document. | | `not_applicable`
The customer has no email, such as the final consumer: the files exist, nothing is sent. |
DeliveryStatus.title: DeliveryStatus

DeliveryStep.description:
The three steps of the customer delivery, in order. Each one runs as one queued job. | | |---| | `attached_document`
Build the AttachedDocument (signed invoice and ApplicationResponse) and sign it. | | `pdf`
Draw the PDF, the graphic representation of the invoice, from its frozen copies. | | `email`
Package the AttachedDocument and the PDF in a zip and email it to the customer. |
DeliveryStep.title: DeliveryStep

HTTP 5xx: the service failed before processing the request. | | `invalid_response`

ElectronicStatus.description:
State machine of the electronic document of an issued invoice. Each step of the chain runs as a queued job that locks the document, checks it is in the state the step expects and moves it on: pending → generated → signed → sending → accepted ↘ rejected → pending (Resend) any step ↘ failed → pending | generated | signed (Retry now, from the step that failed) While sending, a transmission that failed for a transient reason waits for its next attempt; the attempt number and the time of the next one are kept on the document. Drafts have no state. In this project the DIAN is always the local simulator, so accepted and rejected mean "by the * local simulator", never by the DIAN. | | |---| | `pending`
Issued; the XML is about to be generated. | | `generated`
UBL XML built and stored, not signed yet. | | `signed`
Signed with the company certificate and stored; about to be sent. | | `sending`
Being sent, or waiting for the next attempt after a transient failure. | | `accepted`
Accepted by the local DIAN simulator, possibly with notifications. | | `rejected`
Rejected by the rules of the local DIAN simulator; it can be sent again with Resend. | | `failed`
A step failed, or every transmission attempt did; Retry now starts again from that step. |
